findings.description: The DB password (var.password) is interpolated directly into the EC2 instance's user_data, where it is rendered into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc in plaintext and also visible to anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute. Secrets in user_data are stored in instance metadata and are readable by the instance and by API callers.
publicly_accessible = true assigns a public IP/DNS to the RDS instance, exposing the MySQL endpoint to the internet and increasing the attack surface for brute-force and exploitation attempts.
storage_encrypted = false means the RDS data, snapshots, and backups are stored unencrypted at rest, allowing anyone with access to the underlying storage or snapshots to read the data.
The master username is the well-known default 'admin', which combined with a single shared password facilitates credential guessing and brute-force against the database.

The policy grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource '*' to the instance role, giving the EC2 instance full control over the account's S3 buckets, EC2 instances, and RDS databases. Any compromise of the app server results in full account compromise. This is far beyond the permissions needed to connect to the database.

The inbound rule opens TCP/3306 to the entire VPC CIDR (aws_vpc.portal_vpc.cidr_block) rather than a specific application security group, allowing any resource in the VPC — including the public-facing web server — to reach the database port.

The egress rule allows all outbound traffic (protocol -1, port 0, 0.0.0.0/0) from the database security group, permitting data exfiltration and outbound C2 communication if the database host is compromised.

The catalog_db_endpoint output (together with catalog_app_public_dns) exposes internal database connectivity details via the Terraform state and any consumer of the outputs, aiding reconnaissance. Terraform state also holds the plaintext DB password, which is why state must be treated as a secret.

findings.issue_category: credentials written to disk in plaintext
findings.description: The user_data script writes the database server, username, and password into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc under the web root. If PHP handling fails or the directory listing is enabled, the file containing the DB password may be served over HTTP.

The instance does not set metadata_options to require IMDSv2 (HttpTokens = required). With IMDSv1 available, an SSRF or request-forgery vulnerability in the PHP application could read instance credentials and user_data (including the DB password).
